title: A transit-weighted eccentric model gives a 23-day moment fit for 28 HD 139139 dips under a solar-host assumption
abstract: We test a common-orbit-size eccentric population against 28 published HD 139139 dip durations. Geometric transit selection gives a moment ratio that estimates orbital size without an eccentricity term. For a solar mass and radius, the measured moments give eccentricity 0.676 and period 22.91 days. A fitted-distribution simulation gives a tail fraction of 0.082. The fit alone cannot explain the lack of repeats. It also cannot exclude long periods: at a true 88.1-day period and eccentricity 0.80 or 0.90, 17.1 or 43.8 percent of simulated 28-event samples give a period estimate this short. This tests the estimator, not the joint data fit. Selection, host density, finite cloud size, instrument effects and exact high-eccentricity geometry remain open. No new event or planet is found. Original code, aggregate results, two figures and exact external-source retrieval steps are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Transit-selected population predictions and the mean-duration period relation for a solar host.
A specified long-period model can give a short moment estimate in samples of 28 events. This is a marginal estimator check.
